section_summary: This section follows U.S. efforts to protect Alaskan salmon fisheries while Japanese vessels pursued crab fishing in the Bering Sea. Embassy officers urged early talks with Japanese fishery authorities, but the Bureau of Fisheries deferred a proposed visit by Commissioner O’Malley. Later reports track the Nagato Maru and describe other Japanese activity in the Aleutians.

subfiles.title: Despatch on Japanese fishing in Alaskan waters, conclusion
subfiles.about: Japanese officials and packers discuss whether vessels will fish off Alaska in 1931.
subfiles.summary: The Crab Canners’ Guild promises to send no vessels, while officials say independent trawlers are also unlikely to sail.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Embassy despatch of February 9
subfiles.about: State forwards the Tokyo Embassy’s report on Japanese fishing in Alaskan waters.
subfiles.summary: Requests Commerce’s information and comment.

subfiles.title: Correction to despatch No. 134
subfiles.about: The Embassy replaces an erroneous page describing Japanese trawl nets and operations.
subfiles.summary: The corrected page gives net dimensions, catches, vessel distances from shore and Japanese reports of little salmon catch.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of corrected Embassy despatch
subfiles.about: State sends Commerce despatch No. 146 and its corrected enclosure.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the correction concerning Japanese fishing in Alaskan waters.

subfiles.title: Future fisheries and fur-seal arrangements
subfiles.about: Neville urges early consideration of Bering Sea fishery and fur-seal arrangements.
subfiles.summary: He expects Japanese fishing to resume if profitable and suggests discussing conservation and fur seals before business interests become entrenched.

subfiles.title: Note on Neville’s proposal
subfiles.about: A State Department officer assesses Neville’s proposed fisheries consultation.
subfiles.summary: Supports a visit to Tokyo by O’Malley or a trusted representative.

subfiles.title: Neville’s personal letter to Miller
subfiles.about: Neville informally forwards his suggestion to Commissioner O’Malley.
subfiles.summary: Explains why he made the proposal privately and includes personal news.

subfiles.title: Neville’s letter to O’Malley
subfiles.about: Neville proposes direct U.S.–Japanese discussion of Pacific fisheries and fur seals.
subfiles.summary: He describes Japanese conservation interests, pressure on the Robben Island seal rookery and the value of a discreet fisheries visit.

subfiles.title: O’Malley correspondence forwarded to Miller
subfiles.about: O’Malley forwards his answer to Neville and welcomes further suggestions.
subfiles.summary: He thanks State for its handling of Japanese fishery and fur-seal matters.

subfiles.title: O’Malley’s reply to Neville
subfiles.about: O’Malley responds to proposals about Alaskan fishing, seals and a visit to Japan.
subfiles.summary: He welcomes the apparent pause in Japanese fishing, discusses seal population control and says he will consider a visit.

subfiles.title: Note on Forbes telegram
subfiles.about: A State officer reports passing Forbes’s warning to the Bureau of Fisheries.
subfiles.summary: Bowers will forward the telegram to O’Malley while he is away.

subfiles.title: Forbes warns of expanded Japanese fishing
subfiles.about: Forbes urges action before Japanese Bering Sea fishing expands.
subfiles.summary: He expects greater activity next year and warns against waiting for disputes.

subfiles.title: Forbes telegram forwarded to Commerce
subfiles.about: State sends Commerce Forbes’s warning about Alaskan fisheries.
subfiles.summary: Promises to forward the related Embassy despatch when received.

subfiles.title: Forbes urges immediate informal talks
subfiles.about: Forbes asks for a U.S. fisheries representative to visit Japan soon.
subfiles.summary: He considers the moment favorable for informal negotiations.

subfiles.title: Note on telegrams to the Bureau of Fisheries
subfiles.about: State reports notifying the Bureau of Fisheries of Forbes’s telegrams.
subfiles.summary: Bowers expects a delayed response because O’Malley is away.

subfiles.title: State reply on O’Malley’s absence
subfiles.about: State acknowledges Forbes’s fisheries telegrams.
subfiles.summary: The messages have gone to the Bureau of Fisheries while O’Malley is away.

subfiles.title: Nagato Maru voyage announced
subfiles.about: Forbes reports that the Nagato Maru will conduct experimental crab canning off Alaska.
subfiles.summary: Japanese officials say it is the only vessel going and has instructions against interference.

subfiles.title: April 17 telegrams forwarded to Commerce
subfiles.about: State transmits Forbes’s two latest fisheries telegrams.
subfiles.summary: The enclosures cover proposed talks and the Nagato Maru’s sailing.

subfiles.title: Note awaiting Booth’s report
subfiles.about: A State officer recommends waiting for Booth’s report from American packers.
subfiles.summary: Concurs with Bower’s suggestion to defer action on the despatch.

subfiles.title: Proposed Japanese–American crab packing venture
subfiles.about: Forbes reports Iwakura and Booth’s plan for joint packing and marketing of Alaskan crab.
subfiles.summary: Japanese canners propose to supply floating canneries and labor, while American interests supply finance and materials and distribute the crab.

subfiles.title: Bowers discusses O’Malley’s possible Japan visit
subfiles.about: Bowers reports that O’Malley is considering an autumn visit to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The trip might follow a Honolulu visit; State encourages it, and Bowers promises a definite answer.

subfiles.title: Summons to Dooman for consultation
subfiles.about: State asks Dooman to come to Washington for fisheries consultations.
subfiles.summary: Offers a three-day assignment before O’Malley leaves for the summer.

subfiles.title: Dooman’s availability
subfiles.about: Dooman answers the request for a Washington meeting.
subfiles.summary: He can arrive early Friday.

subfiles.title: Conference appointment for Dooman
subfiles.about: State confirms Dooman’s consultation appointment.
subfiles.summary: Sets Friday at 11 a.m. and authorizes travel expenses.

subfiles.title: Conference with Bowers on Alaskan fishing
subfiles.about: Dooman, Miller and Bowers review prospects for a Japanese fisheries understanding.
subfiles.summary: Dooman urges a technical representative to visit Japan and explore conservation measures before Japanese investment grows. Bowers says O’Malley prefers Japanese officials to come to Washington.

subfiles.title: Approval note for Dooman consultation
subfiles.about: A State officer seeks approval to recall Dooman briefly for fisheries talks.
subfiles.summary: Castle has approved the proposal; three days are thought sufficient.

subfiles.title: Memorandum recommending technical talks in Japan
subfiles.about: State assesses the Bureau of Fisheries’ response to Embassy proposals.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum urges a qualified U.S. fisheries official to consult Japanese counterparts, encourage Japanese crab marketing and confer with Booth. It recommends bringing Dooman to Washington to obtain a Bureau decision.

subfiles.title: Copy of Tokyo telegram sent to Bower
subfiles.about: State sends Bower the telegram issued after the fisheries conference.
subfiles.summary: Provides a copy for his files.

subfiles.title: June fisheries conference with O’Malley
subfiles.about: State and fisheries officials discuss safeguards for Alaskan salmon.
subfiles.summary: Dooman explains Japanese willingness to cooperate if compensated. O’Malley considers fur-seal concessions but hesitates to travel; he agrees to consider a Japan visit after an autumn Alaska trip.

subfiles.title: Prospective O’Malley visit reported to Tokyo
subfiles.about: State reports that O’Malley may visit Japan late in 1931.
subfiles.summary: The visit depends on circumstances; details will follow by pouch.

subfiles.title: Conference memoranda sent to Tokyo
subfiles.about: State transmits three memoranda on Japanese fishing off Alaska.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the May 20, May 25 and June 6 memoranda.

subfiles.title: Nagato Maru sighting near Unimak Island
subfiles.about: Commerce reports a June 28 sighting of the Nagato Maru.
subfiles.summary: The vessel and smaller craft were seen about five miles off Unimak Island, apparently packing crab.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Nagato Maru report
subfiles.about: State acknowledges Commerce’s report of the Nagato Maru sighting.
subfiles.summary: The Ambassador has been asked for comment and the ship’s departure date.

subfiles.title: Inquiry to Tokyo about Nagato Maru
subfiles.about: State requests comment on the Nagato Maru’s reported Alaskan operations.
subfiles.summary: Asks when the cannery left Japan.

subfiles.title: Japanese vessels reported near Amak Island
subfiles.about: Commerce forwards Captain Schulz’s account of Japanese vessels and nets near Amak Island.
subfiles.summary: Schulz describes launches, a steamer and a buoyed net observed from the Chirikof on August 1.

subfiles.title: Amak Island report forwarded to Tokyo
subfiles.about: State transmits Commerce’s report of Japanese fishing near Amak Island.
subfiles.summary: Sends the August 19 letter for the Embassy’s information.

subfiles.title: Reminder to Tokyo about Alaskan fisheries
subfiles.about: State directs the Embassy to earlier fisheries communications.
subfiles.summary: Cites the June 6 telegram and June 8 instruction.

subfiles.title: Request for Nagato Maru track chart
subfiles.about: Commerce seeks detailed evidence of the Nagato Maru’s movements.
subfiles.summary: Requests a track chart and information on any activity in U.S. coastal waters.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of track-chart request
subfiles.about: State acknowledges Commerce’s request for an investigation of the Nagato Maru.
subfiles.summary: The Ambassador has been asked to investigate and report.

subfiles.title: Nagato Maru investigation requested in Tokyo
subfiles.about: State sends Commerce’s request for details of the Nagato Maru’s operations.
subfiles.summary: Directs the Ambassador to investigate and report.

subfiles.title: Nagato Maru departure from Hakodate
subfiles.about: Forbes answers the inquiry about the Nagato Maru’s departure.
subfiles.summary: He reports no change in plans and says the ship sailed from Hakodate on May 2.

subfiles.title: Blueprint of Japanese fishing location
subfiles.about: Commerce forwards a chart of Japanese fishing observed by Captain Schulz.
subfiles.summary: The Alaska Packers Association supplied the blueprint.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of fishing-location blueprint
subfiles.about: State acknowledges receipt of the fishing-location blueprint.
subfiles.summary: Thanks Commerce for the chart showing Schulz’s 1931 observation.

subfiles.title: Coast Guard report forwarded by Treasury
subfiles.about: Treasury sends a confidential Coast Guard report on Japanese activity in the Aleutians.
subfiles.summary: Copies also went to Naval Intelligence and Fisheries.

subfiles.title: Japanese activities along the Aleutian Islands
subfiles.about: The Bering Sea Patrol compiles interviews about Japanese ships and visitors in the Aleutians.
subfiles.summary: Witnesses recount visits by the Hakuho Maru and Kokusai Maru, including fishing inquiries, photography and interactions with island residents. The report also notes the Nagato Maru’s crab-canning season in Bristol Bay.

subfiles.title: Nagato Maru’s departure from Bering Sea
subfiles.about: Neville reports the result of an inquiry into the Nagato Maru.
subfiles.summary: He could learn only that it left the Bering Sea for home on September 30.

subfiles.title: Neville’s report forwarded to Commerce
subfiles.about: State forwards Neville’s report on the Nagato Maru.
subfiles.summary: Encloses Embassy despatch No. 373.

subfiles.title: Forbes asks when O’Malley will visit
subfiles.about: Forbes asks whether O’Malley will reach Japan before the next fishing season.
subfiles.summary: He says a prompt visit is advisable if talks are to accomplish anything.

subfiles.title: Bowers reports no visit planned
subfiles.about: Miller records Bowers’s answer about O’Malley’s proposed visit.
subfiles.summary: O’Malley plans no action, citing economy and other considerations.

subfiles.title: Tokyo informed of deferred fisheries action
subfiles.about: State replies to Forbes’s question about O’Malley.
subfiles.summary: Reports that no further action is contemplated at present.

subfiles.title: Illegible Far Eastern Affairs file note
subfiles.about: A heavily degraded note appears to concern Forbes and Commerce.
subfiles.summary: Its substantive recommendation cannot be recovered confidently from the OCR.

subfiles.title: Forbes’s personal appeal to Castle
subfiles.about: Forbes urges Castle to revive talks on Alaskan fisheries.
subfiles.summary: He argues that delay could allow investments and disputes to grow, and questions postponing O’Malley’s trip for economy while attention is focused on Manchuria.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Ensenada vessel report
subfiles.about: A file note points to a report on a Japanese fishing vessel in Ensenada harbor.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references file 894.20212/326 for the February 19 incident.

subfiles.title: Review of Japanese fishing activities in Alaskan waters
subfiles.about: State reviews the history and stalled status of fisheries discussions with Japan.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum traces Commerce’s 1930 warning, Embassy talks and proposals for O’Malley to visit Japan. It concludes that Commerce has dropped the trip and plans no near-term action.
